newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Nordbanken higher 9 mo profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Nordbanken higher 9 mo profit.

text.p: Sweden's Nordbanken is expected to post a profit after credit losses of 5.49 billion crowns for the first nine months of 1996, a Reuter poll of 10 analysts showed on Friday.
This compared to a profit after credit losses of 4.55 billion crowns in the corresponding period a year ago.
The average forecast for credit losses was 515 million crowns against 966 million a year earlier. Forecasts varied between 450-560 million crowns.
For the full year 1996 Nordbanken was expected to post a profit of 6.98 billion crowns after credit losses. This compared to 5.09 billion in 1995.
Analysts forecast full year credit losses at between 600-900 million crowns.
For 1997 analysts forecast profit after credit losses at 6.29 billion crowns. Forecast varied between 5.20 bilion and 7.10 billion crowns.
For 1998 analysts forecast a profit of 6.41 billion crowns on average. Forecasts came in between 5.30-7.25 billion crowns.
Analysts questioned for the poll were from Enskilda, Morgan Stanley, SBC Warburg, Ohman, James Capel, Penser FK, Fiba Nordic, Aragon, Handelsbanken Markets, and Aros.
Nordbanken's nine month report is due to be released on October 30.
NOTE - Earnings are profit before credit losses and operating result after credit losses.
